title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans
title_zh: 小鼠与人类肌腱/韧带干细胞的鉴定
abstract: Ligamentum flavum (LF) hypertrophy resulting in spinal cord compression is a key cause of lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). There are no medical therapies for LSS, in part because the identity of the tendon/ligament stem cell (TLSC) mediating LSS remains unclear. Here, we identify the TLSC present in all tendons and ligaments in humans and mice as Lin-Thy1.2-Sca-1-CD73+CD140α- cells that display self-renewal and give rise to all other tenocyte lineage cells. This TLSC also sits at the apex of their differentiation hierarchy, as determined by in vivo somatic-variant-based lineage tracing. LSS induction led to druggable, calcium signaling-dependent, cell-intrinsic reprogramming of the TLSCs to increase their tenocyte output. Overall, this work identifies the TLSC and establishes dysregulated differentiation of this cell as a mechanism contributing to LSS. This TLSC is anticipated to play a central role in other disorders of tendons and ligaments.
abstract_zh: 黄韧带（LF）肥大导致脊髓压迫是腰椎狭窄（LSS）的主要原因。目前缺乏针对LSS的医学治疗，部分原因在于介导LSS的肌腱/韧带干细胞（TLSC）的身份尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们在人体和小鼠的所有肌腱和韧带中鉴定出TLSC，其表型为Lin‑Thy1.2‑Sca‑1‑CD73+‑CD140α-细胞，具有自我更新能力，并能分化为所有其他肌腱细胞谱系。通过体内体细胞变异基线追踪，进一步证明该TLSC位于其分化层级的顶端。诱导LSS后，TLSC经历可药物靶向、钙信号依赖的细胞内重编程，导致其肌腱细胞产出增加。总体而言，本研究识别了TLSC，并确立了该细胞分化失调是导致LSS的机制之一。预计该TLSC在其他肌腱和韧带疾病中也将发挥核心作用。
